transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-01-25 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (CTO), Sofia (Cloud Eng), Marcus (Sec), Dana (PM)

Summary: Short discovery focused on Aurora Payments' requirements for a private deployment in AWS, constraints around region/residency, VPC connectivity options (peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway), and security/KMS requirements. Next steps agreed: share network diagram, security docs, schedule technical deep dive and benchmark.

Topics: private VPC onboarding, VPC peering, interface endpoints / PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, cross-account roles, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2/compliance, egress/ingress rules, region constraints (eu-west-1 primary), routing tables and NATs, model hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

[00:00] Jordan: All right, uh good afternoon everyone, this is Jordan from Redwood, thanks for taking the time. we have Priya here from the solutions engineering side.
[00:09] Priya: hi all, quick intro from me i do infra and private deploys, i'll be the technical lead on the call.
[00:15] Liam: hey Jordan, Priya, thanks. we're eager to understand options—whether we can run Redwood in our VPC, what networking looks like, and the security tradeoffs.
[00:25] Jordan: perfect, we'll do a quick discovery then dive into the networking details and gaps. dh, dana?
[00:30] Dana: yeah, i'm the product lead, happy to chime in on use cases.
[00:34] Jordan: great. so first, could you give a sense of your current infra footprint and the primary constraints?
[00:42] Sofia: sure. Aurora runs primarily in eu-west-1 and we're trying to keep all PHI and payment processing metadata within EU. we have a multi-account AWS setup: one dedicated infra account, a few app accounts. VPCs are peered via Transit Gateway currently.
[00:56] Marcus: from security side we need full audit logs, KMS for keys, SSO integration (SAML/Okta), RBAC. also strict egress rules, we only allow outbound via specific NATs and have a proxy layer.
[01:11] Priya: ok that helps. for Redwood Private, we support deploying our control plane in your VPC or we can run a private control plane with private endpoints depending on the model. just to clarify: you want the inference runtime to live inside your network, correct?
[01:29] Liam: yes inference inside our VPC for data residency and to avoid exfil. we also want minimal public endpoints.
[01:36] Jordan: good. quick note - there are multiple patterns: 1) full Private deployment (control plane in your env, inference nodes inside your accounts), 2) Dedicated with VPC peering / PrivateLink back to Redwood's infra, or 3) Hosted with strict IP allowlist. each has tradeoffs on ops burden and latency.
[01:55] Sofia: can you walk through peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway? we've got TGW already.
[02:02] Priya: sure. VPC peering is simple but scale is limited cross account, doesn't support transitive routing. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives you an endpoint service and private ENIs, good for private API endpoints and works cross-account, and Transit Gateway is great for central routing at scale — we often integrate with TGW for enterprise customers. given you have TGW, that is usually the recommended path for predictable routing.
[02:29] Marcus: what about IP ranges? our VPCs use RFC1918 but some overlap concerns with Redwood test envs.
[02:35] Priya: we'll provide guidance on non-overlapping ranges. for cross-account PrivateLink we don't need peering if you use interface endpoints. we can also accept peered routes — we usually ask for a list of route tables where the endpoints should be reachable.
[02:49] Jordan: additionally, we support AWS PrivateLink for our control plane endpoints, and for inference nodes we recommend deploying in customer's accounts (we provide an AMI/terraform) that attaches to your subnets and security groups. that removes public traffic.
[03:03] Liam: is there an option to have Redwood-managed infra but within our VPC? like we don't want to run the nodes ourselves but still keep traffic in VPC.
[03:11] Priya: yep, we offer a managed Private deployment where Redwood operates the nodes in a dedicated account but the networking is via VPC peering or TGW attachments; for highest isolation we can do customer-owned subnets with cross-account roles. tradeoff: managed is faster to start, self-hosted gives you more control.
[03:27] Dana: timeline is tight for us — we want a pilot in 6 weeks. is that feasible?
[03:33] Jordan: for a pilot yes; typically we spin up a small dedicated pool or a private test cluster. we need network access, a few firewall rules, and IAM cross-account role for S3 if you're providing models or datasets.
[03:44] Priya: and for benchmarks we usually ask for a baseline: expected QPS, avg sequence length, token mix. that helps pick instance types and quantization profile.
[03:53] Sofia: QPS will be low initially, like 2-5 rps, spikes maybe 20 during peak, seq length 512 typical.
[04:01] Priya: perfect, that's lightweight, we can do a small MPS/GPU pool.
[04:05] Marcus: security — do you integrate with customer KMS and support HSM-backed keys? logs to our SIEM?
[04:12] Priya: yes we support CMKs in customer accounts and can integrate with HSM-backed keys. logs — we can forward audit logs to your S3 or direct to CloudWatch/EventBridge and you can ingest to your SIEM. we also support syslog forwards for some customers.
[04:25] Jordan: for SOC2 and compliance, we'll send the attestation pack. note: if you require dedicated network isolation + audited control plane we recommend Private with customer-owned subnets.
[04:36] Liam: region constraints — are all Redwood images and runtime options available in eu-west-1?
[04:41] Priya: most of our common GPU instance types are available there; a couple of specialized SKUs might be limited but we can recommend compatible instance types and quantization to reduce memory. we also have a model catalog with verified profiles per region.
[04:54] Sofia: about private endpoints — do we need to open outbound to the internet for model downloads/updates?
[05:00] Priya: we can pull images from your private S3 (cross-account role) or we can stage artifacts in an S3 bucket behind VPC endpoints. if you prefer no internet egress we can support an air-gapped workflow where we push the runtime via your Ops team or a secured S3 transfer.
[05:15] Marcus: what's the authentication flow? SSO to console plus service accounts for API keys?
[05:20] Jordan: console SSO integrates with SAML/Okta for UI access. API auth for service-to-service is via short-lived tokens minted by Redwood control plane; for Private you can surface tokens via your IDP or we can integrate with STS assume-role flows.
[05:33] Dana: on auditing, can we see per-token cost and per-request latency breakdown?
[05:38] Priya: yes Redwood Console includes token-level cost breakdown and tracing. we can stream audit events to your account as well.
[05:45] Liam: regarding network ports, firewall etc — what exactly needs to be whitelisted?
[05:50] Priya: depends on pattern. For Private with nodes in your VPC almost nothing outbound. For managed nodes we ask for a few control-plane endpoints (PrivateLink or specific IP ranges) on TLS 443, and health check ports for our agents if you allow internal. we'll provide a concise list.
[06:06] Jordan: i'll add that to the next steps; we'll give a minimal inbound/outbound port list and example security group.
[06:12] Sofia: any gotchas with TGW attachments and route propagation? we use route propagation to many spoke VPCs.
[06:19] Priya: with TGW we'll ask which route tables are propagated and ensure there are no overlapping CIDRs. if you rely on proxy appliances in between, we may need static routes or an extra hop for logging.
[06:32] Marcus: latency — we need 95th < 250ms for core checks. can you meet that running in eu-west-1?
[06:39] Priya: typically yes if compute is colocated in the same AZ/region. network path adds variability; that's why private deployment inside customer's VPC is best for predictable latency. quantization/half precision can also speed up token generation.
[06:52] Liam: cost question: what are the unit economics differences between Dedicated and Private?
[06:57] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood-managed infra — predictable monthly commit with lower ops overhead. Private (customer-hosted nodes) shifts infra cost to you but lowers per-token fees; managed Private blends both: you pay a platform fee and a managed ops premium. we'll include sample numbers for your projected QPS.
[07:17] Dana: what about rollback and model updates? we want canary rollouts and automatic fallback.
[07:22] Priya: supported — per-route rollouts, canary and A/B, model pinning. in Private we surface the same rollout controls to your control plane.
[07:31] Jordan: ok let's go through an example network pattern (Priya you can run the diagram)
[07:36] Priya: (describes) you have account A (infra) and account B (apps). we create a Redwood service account or use your account to run agents; for Private managed we create TGW attachment from Redwood account to your TGW or create a PrivateLink service in your infra account and you create interface endpoints in the spokes. advantage of PrivateLink is no route propagation issues, advantage of TGW is central control.
[08:02] Sofia: do we need cross-account IAM roles for S3/CloudWatch?
[08:07] Priya: yes, we'll ask for a role ARN to assume for artifact pulls and logs. we can also use external ID for security.
[08:14] Marcus: encryption at rest and in transit?
[08:17] Priya: in transit TLS 1.2+, at rest we default to customer CMKs when provided, otherwise Redwood-managed keys. HSM is supported for stricter compliance.
[08:29] Jordan: any other stakeholders we should loop in?
[08:32] Liam: our networking lead Owen should be on the deep dive; also InfoSec will want to review SOC docs, so Marcus will coordinate.
[08:40] Jordan: great. i'll include Owen in scheduling.
[08:43] Dana: what about region failover? we have DR plans in another eu region.
[08:49] Priya: we can replicate artifacts across regions and stand up a failover cluster. there are tradeoffs around async caching and KV cache warmup — we'll document cold-start behaviours.
[08:59] Sofia: curious about metrics retention and access logs — retention in our S3 or Redwood's?
[09:05] Priya: retention can be configured — we can stream logs into your S3 or keep in Redwood for convenience; for enterprise we often hand over retention to the customer account.
[09:15] Jordan: quick pause for questions from the team?
[09:20] Liam: one more on endpoint DNS — do private endpoints require internal DNS records?
[09:25] Priya: yes for PrivateLink you'll have ENIs with private DNS optional. For TGW attachments we rely on normal VPC DNS; we can provide a CNAME pattern for service discovery.
[09:37] Marcus: any perf benchmarks you can share for eu-west-1 gpus?
[09:41] Priya: yes we'll share our region-specific benchmark sheet and a recommended starter instance type.
[09:47] Dana: ok, i'm comfortable with pilot approach. 6 weeks is acceptable pending network review.
[09:53] Jordan: excellent. to summarize next steps: we'll send network diagram and security pack, Priya will draft benchmark plan and firewall rules, and we'll schedule the deep dive with your networking lead.
[10:05] Sofia: sounds good. one last admin: how does billing work for pilot?
[10:10] Jordan: for pilots we often do usage-based billing or a short committed monthly for Dedicated. we'll propose options in the pricing doc.
[10:18] Dana: perfect.
[10:20] Jordan: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar for the technical deep dive.

End of transcript.

References / Links mentioned: "Private deployment checklist (link)"; "SOC2 attestation (link)"; "Region-specific benchmarks (link)"
